summary:
Pernambuco recorded 7 killings of trans and travesti people in 2025, the second-highest raw count of any Brazilian state in the ANTRA dossier released on 26 January 2026, behind Ceará and Minas Gerais at 8 each, against a national total of 80. In a state of some 9.1 million people that is roughly 0.08 per 100,000 residents. SBT News reported the figures on 26 January 2026, Valor Internacional on 27 January 2026, and Diario de Pernambuco carried the state ranking on the same date. The ranking is by raw count alone; the sources provide no per-capita comparison between states.

The 2025 figure is Pernambuco's lowest annual count since 2022, when 13 trans and travesti people were killed, after 9 in 2023 and 8 in 2024. The same dossier records 83 violent deaths of trans people in Pernambuco over six years, the sixth-highest state total for that period, and 349 killings across the Northeast from 2017 to 2025.

Killings are concentrated outside the Recife capital region. On 2 October 2025 a trans woman was shot dead inside her home in Belo Jardim, in the Agreste interior; the Civil Police opened an inquiry to identify the author and motive and no arrests had been reported at publication. On 7 July 2021 Fabiana da Silva Lucas, a 30-year-old Black trans woman, was found dead along highway PE-160 in Santa Cruz do Capibaribe, killed by several knife strikes, the third recorded killing of a trans or travesti person in the state that month. Pernambuco's Civil Police told press that a 22-year-old suspect was lynched by locals at the scene.

Pernambuco stands under Brazil's national legal framework, which the Brazil record carries; the state layer adds its own instruments. The Legislative Assembly of Pernambuco's president signed Law No. 18,634 on 13 July 2024, instituting the State Policy for Combating Violence against LGBTQIA+ People, approved on 4 July 2024. It treats violence based on gender identity, sexual orientation and sex characteristics as structural and incompatible with democratic rule, and requires the state to monitor violence data with a compiled methodology, build protection and reception services, map and train public and civil-society reception facilities, and prioritise victims facing rupture of family or community ties and compounded vulnerabilities.

Municipal hostility has been documented and reversed. On 13 December 2017 Garanhuns enacted Municipal Law No. 4432/2017 banning discussion of gender theory or identity in municipal schools, passed 11-to-1 despite a state prosecution recommendation to reject it as reinforcing stereotypes and prejudice. On 15 October 2025 the Supreme Federal Court struck the law down, lifting the ban on gender-related instruction in the city's schools.

The state judiciary has applied national document-recognition rules locally. In 2023, following a 2022 lawsuit by the Public Defender's Office of Pernambuco, the Court of Justice of Pernambuco authorised Tarlazza Messina to rectify their birth certificate to register gender as non-binary, the first such recognition in the state.

In June 2026 state deputy João Paulo (PT) presented Bill No. 4.092/2026 to create a State Policy for Integral Health Promotion of the LGBTQIAPN+ population within the Unified Health System. It would reinforce the right to a social name in registration and care, address travestis and transexuais who delay or avoid care for fear of mistreatment, and require training of health professionals and publication of LGBT health indicators under data-protection rules. The bill's status is unresolved in the sources.
tangentialFactors:
The state ranking is a raw-count ranking. Pernambuco's 7 killings place it second nationally, but the sources give no per-capita or population-adjusted comparison with Ceará, Minas Gerais or any other state, so the ordering cannot be read as a measure of relative danger for a trans visitor.

The 2021 Santa Cruz do Capibaribe case shows two features at once: an interior killing of a Black travesti, and the collapse of ordinary process when a suspect was lynched by a crowd before arrest. That pattern of extra-legal violence sits alongside, rather than inside, the state's formal protection machinery.

Pernambuco's own instruments operate on top of a national anti-discrimination and gender-recognition framework that already applies in the state; the state policy adds monitoring, reception services and a prioritisation duty rather than new prohibitions.
localsOnly:
Law No. 18,634 obliges the Pernambuco executive to regulate the State Policy for Combating Violence against LGBTQIA+ People and to implement it through reception-service guidelines, emergency support to civil-society services, data collection with research bodies and universities, and partnerships with municipalities, with entry into force on publication.

Residents can invoke the policy's priority categories: victims of identity-based violence or discrimination, people facing actual or imminent rupture of family or community ties, and people with intersecting race, territory, class, gender, age, religion or disability vulnerabilities.

The Court of Justice of Pernambuco's 2023 non-binary birth-certificate rectification is a state precedent available to residents seeking gender-marker recognition, obtained through the Public Defender's Office after litigation rather than by administrative application.

Bill No. 4.092/2026 would bind the state's Unified Health System facilities on social-name use, professional training and LGBT health data; until it advances, those commitments are not in force at state level.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Pernambuco-specific rule, unit or documented case governing the placement of trans prisoners in the state's own prison system is sourced here; the placement framework in force in the state is national and is carried on the Brazil record.

The sources give no per-capita comparison between Brazilian states for trans killings, so the state ranking cannot be converted into a relative risk measure.

Implementation of Law No. 18,634 is not evidenced: no regulation, budget line, monitoring report or enforcement action under the policy appears in the inventory.

The legislative status and fate of Bill No. 4.092/2026 after its June 2026 presentation are unresolved in the sources.
